claim: Media Studio v0.2.1 candidate is ready for release: VAAPI/NVENC profiles perform real capability checks, honor configuration fallback policy, discover or accept a valid VAAPI render node, provide observable fallback, and Arch plus experimental Flatpak packaging are bound to v0.2.1 without regressing Dolphin, atomic output, queue, watch, or public install behavior.

output.summary: Rust and direct hardware evidence is positive, but known queue/override and Flatpak defects plus missing source, packaging, and consumer proof prevent release readiness.
material_defects: The Flatpak manifest provides permissions but no ffmpeg, ffprobe, ImageMagick, dialog, KDE cache, or systemd command provision/wrappers. The application resolves these tools directly with which and invokes them directly, so filesystem access alone does not provide the advertised host integration.

Queued and watch executions do not propagate MEDIA_STUDIO_VAAPI_DEVICE. The override is read from the service environment, but queue.rs supplies neither --setenv nor a device argument; direct-run evidence does not prove the Dolphin/user-systemd path honors it.

When a selected hardware encoder fails at runtime, run_ffmpeg_once invokes fallback_args without the target-size rate flags. Hardware fallback with target_size_mb can therefore miss the requested size or exhaust retries.
ffmpeg_encoder_available ignores the ffmpeg probe exit status and parses stderr as well as stdout, allowing a failed capability query containing the encoder token to be treated as available.
evidence_gaps: No flatpak-builder build was run; only YAML parsing and literal tag checks are evidenced.
The v0.2.1 tag was not pushed, and neither package manifest fetches or pins the candidate digest.
No queued/watch test proves MEDIA_STUDIO_VAAPI_DEVICE propagation.
No evidence covers disabled fallback, invalid VAAPI override, target-size hardware fallback, Dolphin menus, queue/watch behavior, collision-safe atomic commits, or install.sh/public assets.
supported_claims: Formatting, 11 Rust tests, clippy, and release build passed according to the bounded evidence.
Direct VAAPI and NVENC runs show a selected VAAPI device, observable NVENC runtime fallback, committed output, and verification.
The source contains exact-token encoder checks, render-node validation, environment/config override precedence, fail-closed branching, and fallback log markers.
Arch parsing and Flatpak YAML/app-id/tag checks passed; the README explicitly labels Flatpak experimental and non-strict.
prohibited_claims: Do not claim the Flatpak host-integration package works.
Do not claim MEDIA_STUDIO_VAAPI_DEVICE works through Dolphin, queue, or watch execution.
Do not claim the package sources are bound to this candidate digest or that public v0.2.1 installation was verified.
Do not claim Dolphin, queue/watch, atomic-output, or public-install non-regression from the supplied evidence.
required_changes: Provide or explicitly wrap the required host tools in Flatpak, then run an actual flatpak-builder and host-integration test.
Propagate the VAAPI device through queued/watch jobs, preserve target-rate flags on runtime fallback, and make the encoder probe fail closed on nonzero status.
Fetch or publish v0.2.1 and verify both manifests against the exact candidate source; perform an actual Arch package build.
Run disabled/invalid hardware tests plus Dolphin, queue/watch, atomic-output, and public installer/release checks.
residual_risks: Flatpak runtime-version: master is unpinned and unbuilt.
The release workflow does not itself verify that the release tag, Cargo version, package sources, and candidate digest match.
